Can you explain the main options in simple terms?
Yep—here are the main options, super simple:
• Unscented Pure Beeswax: basically “just beeswax.” It has a naturally light honey smell (not added fragrance). Great if you’re scent-sensitive. Common styles are pillars (long burn, general use) and tapers (dinner table / décor).
• Scented candles: if you want a noticeable scent. Botanica is pure beeswax scented with essential oils (in glass). Aromática is a stronger-throw option made with clean fragrance + coconut wax.

Is there anything else a beginner needs to get started?
menu
Not much — tea lights are pretty “set it and forget it.” The main thing is to always burn them in the cups they come in (or a snug, fitted tea light holder) on a level, heat-safe surface, and never leave them unattended.
Optional (but helpful): trim the wick to about 1/4" before the first burn, and try to burn for at least ~1.5 hours per session so the wax melts evenly.
